newsitem.title: BULGARIA: SOFIA AIRPORT SEEKS $150 MILLION FOR REBUILDING.
newsitem.headline: SOFIA AIRPORT SEEKS $150 MILLION FOR REBUILDING.

text.p: Bulgaria hopes to start rebuilding Sofia airport next year if it can find investors to fund the development work, the airport's executive director Danyo Adanev said on Friday.
Adanev said the first stage of the long-delayed repairs and reconstruction was expected to cost some $150 million.

"We are prepared to start work in May or June but this depends on finding potential investors as we have started talks with a number of firms showing interest in the airport's development and reconstruction," Adanev told a news conference.

He said feasibility studies for modernising the 56-year-old airport, worked out by a Bulgarian team and two British consulting firms, Gibb Business Consulting and Hallcrow, have been sent to European, U.S. and Japenese banks and big firms.
The first stage of the airport's reconstruction includes enlargement of a passenger terminal to handle 3.5 million passengers per year and a cargo terminal for up to 60,000 tonnes per year, he said.
Adanev said that 1996 had been difficult for Sofia airport due to tough international competition in attracting clients.

This year the airport expects a net profit of 1.2 billion levs, which could not be realistically compared to last year's figures due to the rising inflation and the drastic fall of the lev against the dollar, he said.
The airport's profit last year was 530 million levs.
A total of 54 airlines operated to and from Sofia airport during 1996 and 39 of them were foreign carriers, Adanev said. Last year the operating foreign airlines were 24.
Passenger traffic dropped by 3-4 percent this year to 1.1 million as debt-ridden national carrier Balkan Airlines has cut its flights by 7-8 percent.
Adanev said 54 percent of all the 23,760 planes serviced at the airport during the year belonged to Balkan.
Cargo transportation was expected to total almost 11,000 tonnes, keeping last year's volumes despite the country's economic crisis.
Last month Austrian Airlines started transiting cargo from Vienna to Sofia by planes and from Sofia to Thessaloniki in Greece by trucks.
The airport, 10 km (six miles) from the city centre, has already invested more than 500 million levs for repair work and some $1 million for supplying machines and equipment.
Last year Bulgaria dropped France's Campenon Bernard SGE from a $100 million deal to modernise the airport because of disagreements over financial terms, officials said.
